newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: F&P expects unchanged 1997/98 profit.
newsitem.headline: F&P expects unchanged 1997/98 profit.

text.p: Whiteware manufacturer Fisher & Paykel Ltd said on Friday it expects to report a similar net profit in the March 1997/98 year to the year just passed.
"If sales levels continue as they have started this year we believe that we can achieve a similar profit in fiscal 1998 to fiscal 1997," Chairman Sir Colin Maiden told the annual meeting.
Maiden said this would depend on factors such as volume, price, cost innovation and competitive pressures.
F&P posted a net profit of NZ$37.2 million in the year to March 1997 compared to $39.3 million the year before.
Maiden said it was difficult to predict the performance for the new financial year.
"On one hand we have started the year with increased unit sales. On the other hand we have had to reduce margins to obtain some of those sales."

Maiden said a further decline in confidence in F&P's key markets could negatively affect sales numbers. However, if unit sales continued to rise, F&P would increase production volume in all its factories.

Chief executive Gary Paykel said in the first quarter, unit sales in each month matched unit sales for the corresponding month last year, when retailer Noel Leeming (now part of the Pacific Retail group) withdrew from its distribution network in November.
Then in December, Noel Leeming and affiliate Bond & Bond withdrew from F&P Finance.
"Undoubtedly, this had an impact on our sales in the second half of the financial year but the New Zealand retail market is dynamic," Paykel said.
F&P dealers had responded with an improved level of sales.
In Australia, unit sales growth continued in the first quarter. Whiteware sales to the rest of the world were up slightly with a strong performance from Japanese distributors.
Paykel said the trend continued in July in all key markets.

"Increased unit sales have been at some cost to margins as we have taken a firm decision to respond quickly to new price points established by our competitors in both New Zealand and Australia," he said.
F&P has now launched a new dishwasher product called "dishdrawer", incorporating advanced technology used in F&P's clothes washing machines.
The appliance has two completely separate drawers in a structure the same size as a conventional dishwasher.
